title: Personal storage at work: S3, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, iCloud and Google Drive

videos.script: bia has a spreadsheet of the month's appointments, and the accountant needs it. {{sheet}} The file is too big for e-mail. She has a Google Drive at home. Four minutes later, the accountant has a link. {{link}} Nothing was hacked. But the clinic has just lost every control it had over that file. {{table}} Who can read it, who did read it, and what happens when bia leaves. {{inventory}} This lesson is about storage the company never chose. {{services}} OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box and iCloud all offer a link that opens for anyone. {{bearer}} Such a link is a key written as an address. Whoever holds it holds the file. {{presign}} S3 has the same thing, the presigned URL. You will make one in your lab, and read whose key signed it. {{controls}} Then the controls a company really owns: its tenant, its network, its buckets. {{end}}
